Threat: SQL injection attack by external attacker
Vulnerability: Web application does not use parameterized queries; user input passed directly to database
Treatment Plan: Remediate immediately: enforce parameterized queries/prepared statements across all database calls; deploy a Web Application Firewall (WAF); conduct quarterly code reviews for injection flaws.

Likelihood (1-5): Credential stuffing attack on customer login portal
Impact (1-5): No multi-factor authentication; no account lockout after repeated failed logins
Owner: Implement MFA for all customer accounts; enforce account lockout after 5 failed attempts; deploy rate limiting on the /login endpoint; monitor for anomalous login patterns.

Threat: Third-party payment processor suffers a data breach
Vulnerability: Excessive PII/payment data shared with processor beyond what is needed for transaction
Treatment Plan: Review and minimize data shared with payment processor; ensure processor is PCI-DSS certified; include breach notification obligations in vendor contract; shift liability via contract.

Threat: Ransomware infection via phishing email to admin employee
Vulnerability: Employees have direct database access from workstations; no email filtering for malicious attachments
Treatment Plan: Deploy endpoint detection and response (EDR) on all admin workstations; enforce least-privilege access — admins should not have direct prod DB access; enable automated daily backups stored offline; implement email filtering.

Vulnerability: Application renders user-supplied content without sanitization; session cookies lack HttpOnly and Secure flags
Treatment Plan: Sanitize and encode all user-supplied output; set HttpOnly and Secure flags on session cookies; implement Content Security Policy (CSP) headers; conduct penetration testing.

Threat: Accidental data exposure by misconfigured S3 bucket
Vulnerability: Cloud storage buckets default to public-read; no automated misconfiguration detection
Treatment Plan: Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level; implement AWS Config rule to alert on public buckets; conduct quarterly cloud configuration audits.

Vulnerability: No DDoS protection service in place; application does not auto-scale under sudden traffic spikes
Treatment Plan: Subscribe to AWS Shield Standard (included free); evaluate AWS Shield Advanced for critical periods; configure auto-scaling groups; deploy CloudFront as a buffer layer.

Threat: Insider threat — disgruntled employee exfiltrates customer data
Vulnerability: No data loss prevention (DLP) controls; admin employees have broad access with no activity monitoring
Treatment Plan: Implement role-based access control (RBAC) with least-privilege; enable CloudTrail and audit logging for all admin actions; deploy user behavior analytics (UBA) to flag anomalous access.

Vulnerability: Application deployed in a single AWS region with no failover
Treatment Plan: Evaluate multi-region deployment or at minimum document RTO/RPO targets; implement Route 53 health checks; create and test a disaster recovery runbook.

Threat: Brute force attack on admin login
Vulnerability: Admin panel exposed on public internet; no IP allowlisting; no MFA requirement
Treatment Plan: Restrict admin portal access to corporate VPN/IP allowlist only; enforce MFA for all admin accounts; implement login attempt rate limiting.

Vulnerability: No software composition analysis (SCA) tooling; outdated packages not tracked or patched
Treatment Plan: Integrate SCA tool (e.g., Dependabot or Snyk) into CI/CD pipeline; establish a patch cadence — critical CVEs patched within 7 days, high within 30 days.

Vulnerability: Legacy API endpoints still accepting HTTP (non-TLS) connections
Treatment Plan: Enforce HTTPS-only across all endpoints; implement HSTS headers; disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1; configure automatic HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect.

Threat: Log data contains PII exposed to unauthorized staff
Vulnerability: Logging framework captures full request/response bodies including customer data without masking
Treatment Plan: Audit all log configurations; implement log masking/redaction for PII fields (email, card numbers, addresses); restrict log access to security team only.

Threat: Test environment uses real production customer data
Vulnerability: No data masking process when copying production data to staging/dev environments
Treatment Plan: Implement a data masking/anonymization process for all non-production data copies; prohibit use of real PII in dev/test environments by policy.

Impact (1-5): CDN cache keys do not account for all relevant request headers; no cache integrity validation
Owner: Monitor CDN provider security advisories; review cache key configuration; accept residual risk given low likelihood.
